provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Care family batch. Tiny tickets and enormous supply: a volume booking-tool play, so everything is priced low and fill reminders carry the retention. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Classic, hybrid, volume and mega volume sets compared by look, appointment length and fill timing, plus lash mapping styles like cat eye and doll eye and the patch test before a first set
pageStructurePlus.why: Lash clients book by the look they saw online and can't name it. A set guide gets them into the right appointment length instead of a rushed or overbooked one.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Gel polish, structured gel, acrylic and dip compared, nail art priced by level from simple accents to full hand-painted sets, and the removal fee for another salon's work
pageStructurePlus.why: Nail art clients send an inspiration picture and ask 'how much'. Priced art levels answer that before the DM and stop the awkward surprise at the end.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Brow lamination, tint, wax, threading and henna, what each lasts, how often to rebook, and semi-permanent brow work only where the artist holds the [permit or licence] for it
pageStructurePlus.why: Brow clients mix up lamination, tint and microblading. Explaining them in plain words makes the studio look expert and books the right service.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How much lash retention a fill needs, whether the studio fills another artist's lashes, the nail fix window for lifted or broken nails, and what counts as a full new set
pageStructurePlus.why: Fill disputes are the most common argument in lash and nail studios. Stating the rule before booking protects the artist and the client.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Autoclaved metal tools, single-use files and buffers, pedicure tub liners, how often stations are cleaned and the state board inspection posted at the nail salon
pageStructurePlus.why: Hygiene is the first worry for new nail and lash clients. A studio that shows its process wins the careful ones away from the cheap walk-in place.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Course dates, what the kit includes, class size, practice model requirements, and the studio's own completion certificate stated as exactly that
pageStructurePlus.why: Many lash artists teach. Course pages with dates and deposits turn the studio's reputation into a second income line.

designDirections.name: Set & Fill
designDirections.bestFor: Solo nail techs and lash artists in a suite who need a priced menu and a Book button above everything
designDirections.headlineSample: Lashes, brows and gel nails in {City}. Book your fill.
designDirections.whyItFits: Peach Sorbet's soft rounded type and warm peach feel friendly and light without looking childish, and stacked cards put fill, full set and Book in one tap.

designDirections.name: Nail Art Wall
designDirections.bestFor: Nail art studios and lash artists whose sets go viral and whose clients book from a style
designDirections.headlineSample: Nail art and lash sets in {City}, booked by style
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Sage Spa, fails CTA contrast and is too quiet for nail art. Magenta Signal reads fashion-forward, makes colourful sets pop and passes AA on the Book button.

designDirections.name: Brow Atelier
designDirections.bestFor: Established lash and brow studios with a waitlist, training courses and premium set prices
designDirections.whyItFits: Rosewood's fashion serif and dusky rose make lash and brow work look like a boutique, and a full-bleed hero lets a single set carry the page.

openers.line: The nail studio's Maps listing has great reviews and no website, so someone in {City} searching for soft gel extensions or structured gel nearby can't see a set or a price before they move on.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what would sit behind that button for the nail studio: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your bio link opens a booking app with 'classic', 'hybrid' and 'volume' and nothing explaining the difference. New lash clients guess, then book the wrong appointment length.
openers.hook: Tap their bio link and check whether lash or brow services have descriptions. If they're names only, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A lash set guide that books the right appointment: {demo-link}

openers.line: The lash studio page on your listing still has last year's fill prices. A client who books from that and pays the new price at the end isn't a happy one.
openers.hook: Open their site or listing and find one outdated price or service. Note it exactly.
openers.linkLine: A lash and brow menu you can update by text: {demo-link}

openers.line: I tried your nail salon's site on my phone and the menu loaded as one tiny block of text. Nail appointments get booked from the couch, on a phone.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The nail salon, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Half the comments on your nail art posts are 'how much for this set'. A page with nail art priced by level would answer them before they DM.
openers.hook: Count the 'how much' or 'price?' comments on their last few nail art posts. Mention one.
openers.linkLine: Nail art priced by level, with booking: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your best lash sets are mixed in with promo graphics and reposts. A gallery sorted by set type, classic to mega volume, would let clients point at what they want.
openers.hook: Find one lash or brow post that clearly shows a set type. Name it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Lash and brow work sorted by set type: {demo-link}

openers.line: One of your Google reviews says the lashes lasted longer than anywhere else she'd tried. That review should sit next to the fill price, not three taps away.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about retention, cleanliness or nail art. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Your reviews right next to the lash and nail menu: {demo-link}

openers.line: December parties and spring break trips are when everyone wants fresh nails and lashes the same week. A booking page spreads those fills across the calendar before it jams.
openers.hook: Use this in November or before spring break. Check their posts for 'booked up' or 'holiday slots' mentions.
openers.linkLine: A lash and nail booking page for the busy season: {demo-link}

openers.line: Lash fills get remembered at eleven at night when someone spots a gap in the mirror. If the studio can't be booked then, they find a lash tech who can.
openers.hook: Look for comments like 'any fills this week?' or reviews mentioning last-minute appointments. Note one.
openers.linkLine: A lash studio that books fills at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw the post about hiring a nail tech for the salon. Good techs look at how the salon presents itself online before they send their nail art.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring notice for a nail tech, lash artist or brow artist. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A nail salon page with a join-the-team section: {demo-link}

openers.line: New lash clients walking into an office building for the first time wander the corridors hunting for suite numbers. A first-visit page with the door code and where to park gets them to the chair on time.
openers.hook: Check reviews or posts for 'hard to find' or a suite number. Note the building.
openers.linkLine: A first-visit guide to the lash suite: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your booking post asks for a deposit by payment app before a full lash set. Every one of those is a message to match up by hand.
openers.hook: Look for deposit instructions in their highlights or captions. Don't name the app back to them.
openers.linkLine: A lash booking that takes the deposit itself: {demo-link}

openers.line: Nothing online mentions the studio's licence or how you sanitise tools, and that's what a careful nail or lash client looks for after a bad experience somewhere else.
openers.hook: Look for licence certificates or sanitation posts. Never state a licence number they haven't published.
openers.linkLine: Your licensing and sanitation, shown plainly: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your lash chair seems booked solid by clients on a two-week fill rhythm. That's great until a few relocate, and the next ones find you by searching, not by luck.
openers.hook: Look for 'fully booked' posts or reviews from long-time fill clients. Quote one.
openers.linkLine: Where a new lash client would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is lovely detail work. A set like that should lead the nail or lash gallery so the next client can point at it and book.
openers.hook: Pick their newest nail art, lash set or brow lamination post and name it exactly.

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is lovely detail work.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and only found the booking app and your social pages. I put together a sample studio page with a lash set guide, nail art priced by level and a Book button for fills, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my message got buried under fill requests. Here's the sample studio site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a lash set guide, nail art priced by level, a fill policy stated up front and a sanitation section. If it's not for you, just say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I set up websites and booking for nail, lash and brow studios here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Totally fine, you're mid-set most of the day. Short version: I built a sample page for {Business Name} with a lash set guide, priced nail art and booking, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and menu changes. For a studio like yours I'd normally quote about {Build Price}."
"Most of the value is the booking and the fill reminders. The page makes them look like a real studio."
"Can I call you between clients one day this week? Tell me the gap."

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start when it clears."

objections.handler: "It takes the appointment. It can't explain classic versus volume or price nail art by level. The page does that, then sends them into your booking app ready to book the right slot."

objections.objection: I'm just one tech in a suite.
objections.handler: "That's who this is built for. One lash or nail tech with a clear page looks like a studio people trust with their eyes and hands."
"They find you there, then they want a price and a slot. The page answers 'how much for this set' and books it while you're working."

objections.objection: There's a cheap nail salon on every corner.
objections.handler: "Exactly why the page shows your sanitation, your nail art levels and your fill policy. Careful clients pay more for the studio that explains itself."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's a priced menu, a set guide and booking. A few weeks of fills covers it."

email.subject: Studio site for {Business Name}

{Owner}, I'm clearing the {Business Name} studio demo off my server on Friday.

Should I keep it up for you instead? Just reply yes or no.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, holiday party season is when lash fills and nail sets stack up in the same fortnight. Studios with booking and fill reminders handle it calmer. Thought of you.

The sample is still here and the price hasn't changed. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: This is a volume play. Keep the build to a few weeks of fills and sell the same template to many studios.
Price the lash set guide and nail art levels as the core work; they're what stop the 'how much' DMs.
Fill reminders are the real retention product. Sell them on day thirty, not as an afterthought.
For suite buildings, price each tech's page separately and offer the building a directory.
Keep every monthly add-on below the price of one fill. Techs cancel anything bigger in a slow month.
Training course pages are priced higher than service pages; they sell a ticket many times a fill.

lineItems.description: Max with every set type, mapping styles, appointment lengths and the patch-test booking step.
Max with several art levels, example sets per level once shot, and an inspiration upload on the booking form.
Max when it covers lamination, tint, threading, henna and semi-permanent work with rebooking timing.
Max with different timing for lash fills, gel fills and brow rebooks, tied to the booking calendar.
Max with course dates, kit details, seat limits and deposit capture on their payment account.

lineItems.item: Suite directory card for each tech
lineItems.description: Max when each card links to that tech's booking and a short gallery of their sets.
Max when menu, policies and booking messages are all translated and checked by the owner.

whatElseYouSell.name: Close-up set content session
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One session with a macro lens on finished lash sets and nail art, with each client's OK, fills the studio gallery for months."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, scheduled on a day with several full sets booked.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for the nail and lash studio
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Fresh lash and nail pictures on the Google profile every week with the service named, so people searching for a lash tech nearby see you first."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after each set
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The evening after a new lash set or nail art, while she's still admiring it, the client gets a short text asking for a review."

whatElseYouSell.name: Holiday nail art and lash gift push
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A December push for holiday nail art sets and lash gift certificates, so party week books out early and evenly."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in October, run from mid-November.

whatElseYouSell.name: Prom and bridal lash and nail push
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A spring push for prom and bridal lash sets and nails, with a group booking option for bridesmaids."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in January, run February to April.

whatElseYouSell.name: Suite door sign and lash aftercare cards
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A door sign for the lash suite and aftercare cards with the fill booking code, so the next fill is booked before she leaves."

whatElseYouSell.name: Nail art timelapse reel editing
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "You film the nail art from above while you work; I cut the timelapses into short reels with the set and price named."

withoutAI.route: The lash and nail supply distributor
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The supplier you buy lash trays and gel from sells to every tech in the region and takes orders by DM. Introduce me and I'll build their pro-order site."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Suppliers' customer lists are your prospect lists, and a tech's introduction makes it warm.

withoutAI.route: Esthetics schools that teach lash and brow
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The esthetics school needs practice models for lash and brow classes and finds them by flyer. A model-call page with booking would fill each class."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Schools always need models and enrolments. Alumni techs are trusted introductions.

withoutAI.whoPays: The makeup artist, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The makeup artist who sends brides to you for lash sets books weddings by DM too. I'd build her a page with packages and trial dates."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Bridal beauty vendors refer in a tight circle. One lash artist opens it.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your building is full of nail, lash and brow suites and has no page listing them. I'll build the tenant directory and the vacancy page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Landlords want occupied suites and busy hallways. The tech inside makes the introduction.

withoutAI.whoPays: Each studio, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The waxing studio down the hall shares your brow clients and books from a bio link. Same booking-first layout, different menu."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same clients, same building, almost the same template.

withoutAI.route: Hair stylists in the same building
withoutAI.whoPays: Each stylist, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The hair stylist next to your lash suite saw your page and asked who built it. I'd do theirs with your studio linked."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Neighbours in a suite building see each other's pages daily.

withAI.route: Pro reorder assistant for the lash supply distributor
withAI.pitchLine: "Lash techs message the curls and lengths they're out of, and the assistant drafts the order from the supplier's own catalogue for approval."
withAI.whyItWorks: Techs already reorder by message. Clean orders save the distributor hours a week.

withAI.route: Model-call booking assistant for esthetics schools
withAI.pitchLine: "People asking about free or cheap lash and brow services at the school get the rules, dates and supervision explained and are booked as models."
withAI.whyItWorks: Schools can count filled model slots. It's an easy result to measure and pay for.

withAI.route: Bridal party beauty scheduler for the makeup artist
withAI.pitchLine: "The bride enters the party and the ceremony time, and the makeup artist's planner lays out makeup, lash and nail slots from her vendor list."
withAI.whyItWorks: Makeup artists run the wedding morning. The lash studio is first on her list.

withAI.route: Vacancy question assistant for the beauty suite landlord
withAI.pitchLine: "Nail and lash techs thinking about going solo ask what a beauty suite costs and what's included, and the landlord wakes up to a booked viewing."
withAI.whyItWorks: Each empty suite costs the owner monthly. One new tenant pays for a year.

withAI.route: Regrowth-timed wax reminders for the esthetician
withAI.pitchLine: "The waxing studio's clients get a reminder timed to regrowth, built from the same logic as your lash fill reminders."
withAI.whyItWorks: You built it once for fills. A second studio is configuration, sold through a neighbour.

withAI.route: Missed-call text-back for the hair stylist down the hall
withAI.pitchLine: "When the stylist next to your lash suite misses a call mid-colour, the caller gets a text with booking options drafted from her menu."
withAI.whyItWorks: Every one-chair business misses calls. A suite building is a ready-made cluster.

softwareAI.name: Fill-due texts per lash and nail client
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Two weeks after a lash set, or three after gel nails, the client gets a text with your next fill slots before the gaps show."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs each service's fill timing and access to the booking calendar.

softwareAI.name: Deposits for full lash sets and nail art
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A full lash set or a nail art appointment takes a deposit at booking, so a no-show on a two-hour set still pays something."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: At build, or the first no-show they mention. Needs their deposit rule and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: Nail art price-level responder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A client sends a nail art inspiration picture and gets the likely art level and price range from your own menu, with the final price set by the tech."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, once the nail art levels page is live. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Patch test tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New lash and brow tint clients can't book a full set until their patch test is logged, so it never gets skipped on a busy day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their patch-test rule and booking access.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for the lash and nail studio
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each review gets a short, warm reply drafted in the tech's voice that names the lash set or nail service, ready to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Fill or full set checker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A client uploads a picture of her current lashes and is told whether it looks like a fill or a full set by your rule, with the lash artist confirming before the appointment."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once the fill policy is published. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Lapsed lash and nail client note
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A client who hasn't had a fill or a nail set in a couple of months gets a friendly note and your next openings."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs visit history and an opt-out line.

softwareAI.name: Studio receptionist for calls and DMs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When both hands are holding tweezers, the lash studio's calls and DMs still get answered and the fill still gets booked."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once they trust you. Needs the menu, policies and booking access. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Lash map record per client
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Curl, length, thickness and mapping style saved for every lash client, so each fill matches the set she loved."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the artist's current notes, even if they're on paper.

softwareAI.name: Lash training course booking and waitlist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Lash and brow course seats book with a deposit, the waitlist fills when a class sells out, and students get kit and model reminders."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, only for artists who teach. Needs course dates, prices and seat limits.

softwareAI.name: Caption drafts for nail art posts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Post the nail art or lash set and get a caption in your voice with the service, the level and the next opening named."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs a few past captions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Cancellation backfill texts for the studio
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A Thursday lash fill cancels and clients overdue for a fill get a text offering it, first to book takes the chair."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs booking access and clients who opted in to texts.

softwareAI.name: Gel, lash tray and adhesive stock list
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which gel colours, lash trays and adhesives are running low and get a reorder list before a set has to be rescheduled."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their product list and a habit of logging use.

softwareAI.name: Bilingual reply drafts for the nail salon
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Nail salon owners who'd rather write in Vietnamese or Spanish get client replies drafted in clear English, and the other way round."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, for owners who want it. Needs the menu and policies in both languages. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Nail tech commission report
softwareAI.pitchLine: "For nail salons with techs on commission: each tech's sets, tips and add-ons totalled at the end of the week."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, only for salons with staff. Needs pay rules and booking data.

softwareAI.name: Fill membership billing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Lash fill and gel maintenance clients pay one monthly amount and book their fills without paying each time."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the membership rules and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: Aftercare text in the studio's own wording
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The lash or brow aftercare sheet the studio already hands out arrives by text that evening, so nobody washes a fresh set too soon."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their written aftercare. Sends only their approved text.

softwareAI.name: Course question assistant for lash students
softwareAI.pitchLine: "People asking about the lash course get kit, dates, models and payment answers from the course handbook, and a deposit link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, for artists who teach. Needs the course handbook. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Station schedule for multi-tech nail salons
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which nail tech is on which station and pedicure chair, and which hours still have gaps, across the week."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, for salons with several techs. Needs schedules and the station list.

softwareAI.name: Lash retention trend flag
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients whose lash retention keeps dropping between fills are flagged, so the artist can check aftercare habits before the client blames the set."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, once lash map records hold a few months of fill notes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise fill reminders and the set guide for solo techs
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built fill reminders and a lash set guide for one studio. Every solo lash and nail tech in the city answers the same DMs."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The supply is enormous and the tickets tiny, so a cheap monthly tool is the only way this category pays at scale.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Graduate launch kit for lash training academies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every lash artist who finishes your course leaves with a booking page, a set guide and fill reminders ready to switch on."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Academies sell careers and compete for students. A launch kit is a reason to choose them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member nail salon a booking page template with sanitation and licensing sections built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need renewal reasons, and sanitation trust is a shared member worry.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Nail salon business associations serving immigrant owners
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your members run nail salons and many prefer to work in Vietnamese. A bilingual booking page template with translated policies is a member benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These associations have deep trust with owners who rarely respond to cold pitches.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label nail and lash template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency gets nail and lash clients and builds generic pages. License my template with the set guide and nail art levels built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell them the beauty-specific part.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Trained-artist locator for a lash product maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Clients want a lash artist trained on your products. A locator tied to your course records sends them to the right studio."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Product makers train artists and want proof it sells product.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Educator directory for a gel system maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Nail techs looking for a class on your gel system can't find a local educator. A directory with class dates and booking fixes it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Gel makers grow through educators. A directory fills their classes.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each nail salon location needs its own techs, hours and booking under one brand. I build the location template once."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One owner, many salons, one rollout.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your beauty expo sells nail and lash classes from a flyer. A site with class booking, vendor booths and competition entry sells more."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Expos sell to every tech in the region; your studio client attends and vouches for you.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Girls buying prom dresses ask where to get nails and lashes done. A partner booking page sends them to your beauty partners and makes the boutique the planner."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Boutiques want to own prom season. Sending beauty bookings to partners makes them more useful.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Studios in the next metro over
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New lash and nail studios elsewhere
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Lash techs in towns where my {City} studios don't compete get the same set guide and fill reminders, already running here."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you sell the same template again and again.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Untangle broken nail and lash booking setups
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your booking app lists fills with the wrong lengths and no deposits. I'll fix the lash and nail services so the calendar stops double-booking."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Studios already paying for an app want it to work. A quick fix opens the bigger sale.

upsellLadder.line: "The nail and lash page and the care plan go on one contract, so a new set price is a text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Introduction to the lash and nail supply distributor
